title: Gene × Environment Interaction Visualiser
summary: Name the pattern in a study that sampled only the adverse half of an environmental range, then widen the range and look again. Move the slopes, the crossover and the sampled window yourself.
learningObjectives: Distinguish diathesis-stress, differential susceptibility and vantage sensitivity by the location of the crossover point.
Explain why the range of environments a study sampled can decide which of the three theories it appears to support.
Explain why a significant interaction term does not choose between the three.
State what evidence is needed to claim differential susceptibility rather than vulnerability.
Describe sensitivity as responsiveness in both directions rather than as a defect.
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; every calculation runs in the browser tab, and the tool asks nothing about the person using it.
accessibilityNotes: Native ranges, checkboxes and buttons throughout; sliders announce meaningful values such as 'crossover inside the range'. Charts are hidden from assistive technology and paired with a visible table giving both groups' model-implied outcomes and their difference at three points in the sampled range. The two groups are distinguished by colour, by dash pattern and by a label printed at the end of each line. The pattern the visible data support is stated in words in a live verdict box. Unsampled regions are shaded and described in the readout as a percentage of range sampled. Reduced motion honoured; forced-colours rules provided; usable at 320px and at classroom-projector widths.
readmeTopic: Gene-environment interaction: how the sampled environmental range decides which theory a study appears to support
simulationNotes: Two fictional sensitivity groups, each a straight line in environmental quality with normally distributed noise, generated from a seeded mulberry32 generator. No gene is named and no genotype appears: the grouping variable is a fictional sensitivity score split for display. No disorder, diagnosis, symptom or clinical risk estimate is used and the outcome axis is an unnamed standardised outcome. No value corresponds to any published finding. Straight lines and a two-group split are deliberate simplifications, both stated on the page; no sampling uncertainty or confidence band is shown.
